title: Plots for Sale in Faisal Town Islamabad – Phase 1 & Phase 2
description: Find plots for sale in Faisal Town Islamabad with Phase 1/F-18 and Phase 2/FT-II options, plot sizes, current prices, maps and buyer checks
h1: Plots for Sale in Faisal Town Islamabad
intro:
Faisal Town Islamabad plot searches can refer to two different projects: the established Phase 1/F-18 resale market and the newer Faisal Town Phase 2/FT-II sector-based project.

Start by choosing the correct phase, then compare plot size, exact location, development, possession or payment status, dues and total payable amount. Current availability and asking prices change frequently.
body:
## First choose the correct Faisal Town project

A broad search for a plot in Faisal Town Islamabad can refer to either:

- Faisal Town Phase 1 / F-18
- Faisal Town Phase 2 / FT-II

These are different projects.

They use different maps, naming systems, payment structures and development positions.

Phase 1 is primarily an established resale market using block references.

Phase 2 is a newer sector-based project with sector, enclave, booking and resale inventory.

Before comparing any prices, confirm which project the property belongs to.

## Faisal Town Phase 1 plots for sale

Faisal Town Phase 1 / F-18 has an established residential resale market.

Current project structure includes:

- Block A
- Block B
- Block B-1
- Block C

Blocks A, B and C currently dominate visible resale inventory, while B-1 is a newer addition and should be checked separately for its current booking, development and regulatory position.

Current property portals show substantial plot inventory across Phase 1.

For example, current listings show dozens of plots in each of Blocks A, B and C. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

## Phase 1 plot sizes

Common Phase 1 residential categories include:

- 5 marla
- 8 marla
- 10 marla
- 14 marla
- 1 kanal

Availability differs by block.

Current Phase 1 material shows:

- Block A: 8, 10, 14 marla and 1 kanal
- Block B: 8, 10, 14 marla and 1 kanal
- Block C: 5, 8, 10, 14 marla and 1 kanal
- Block B-1: commonly 5, 8 and 10 marla categories

Always confirm the documented dimensions rather than relying only on the rounded marla label. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

## Current Phase 1 market snapshot

Phase 1 asking prices vary substantially by block, plot size, street and special location.

Current Block B examples include:

- 8 marla around PKR 1.48 crore to PKR 1.85 crore
- 10 marla around approximately PKR 1.92 crore to PKR 2.3 crore

Current Block C examples include:

- 5 marla around approximately PKR 1.15 crore to PKR 1.5 crore
- 10 marla around approximately PKR 2.4 crore

Current Block A listings also include 8-marla asking examples around PKR 2 crore.

These are seller asking prices, not official rates or guaranteed transaction prices. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

## Block A plots for sale

Block A is an established Phase 1 block with active resale inventory.

Current portal data shows more than 50 plot listings in Block A, with residential inventory forming the majority. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

When comparing Block A plots, check:

- plot size
- exact street
- road width
- corner or standard position
- possession
- dues
- access
- surrounding houses
- total purchase cost

Use the dedicated Block A page for more detailed comparison.

## Block B plots for sale

Block B currently has strong active resale inventory.

Current portal data shows around 69 plots for sale, including large numbers of 8- and 10-marla properties. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

Current examples also show how strongly location can affect asking price.

An 8-marla standard or internal plot may be priced differently from an 8-marla corner property even within the same block.

Compare like-for-like inventory.

## Block C plots for sale

Block C currently has particularly strong resale activity and is important for buyers looking for smaller plots.

Current listings include a large number of 5-marla plots together with 8-, 10-marla and larger options. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

A buyer looking specifically for a smaller residential plot may therefore find more choice in Block C than in Block A or Block B.

## What about Block B-1?

Block B-1 is part of the broader Faisal Town Phase 1 structure but is newer than the established A/B/C resale blocks.

Current project-focused material lists 5, 8 and 10-marla residential categories and indicates booking is closed on one current project page. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}

Because B-1 differs from the older resale blocks, buyers should verify:

- current development
- current resale availability
- regulatory status
- transfer position
- outstanding payments

before comparing it directly with established A/B/C inventory.

## Faisal Town Phase 2 plots for sale

Faisal Town Phase 2 / FT-II uses sector and enclave terminology rather than the Phase 1 A/B/C block structure.

Current detailed guides on this website cover:

- Sector O / Model Block
- Sector P / The Caladan
- Sector R
- Sector S
- Sector T
- Overseas Enclave

Phase 2 inventory may include:

- fresh booking
- cash offers
- installment inventory
- numbered plots
- partially paid files
- fully paid files
- resale plots
- NDC-ready inventory

That means two Phase 2 plots of the same size may have completely different financial positions.

## Phase 2 plot sizes

Common Phase 2 residential categories include approximately:

- 5.56 marla
- 8 marla
- 10.89 marla
- 14.22 marla
- 1 kanal
- 2 kanal in selected areas

Not every size is available in every sector.

The exact current inventory should be confirmed on the relevant sector page or current booking documentation.

## Sector O / Model Block plots

Sector O is one of the best-known current Phase 2 areas and is widely associated with the Model Block.

Current listings show active Sector O inventory.

Recent seller listings include approximately:

- 5.56 marla around PKR 27.9 lakh
- 8 marla around PKR 37.3 lakh
- 10.89 marla around PKR 48.5 lakh
- 14.22 marla around PKR 60.6 lakh
- 1 kanal around PKR 81.2 lakh

These examples reflect advertised cash or discounted offers and should not be treated as a permanent official Phase 2 price list. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}

## Sector P / The Caladan

Sector P is marketed as The Caladan and currently has one of the clearest dedicated price structures in the Phase 2 cluster.

For that reason, Sector P prices should remain on the dedicated Sector P page rather than being generalized across all FT-II inventory.

If you are specifically interested in Sector P, compare:

- plot size
- current discount
- exact plot
- premium location
- development charges
- final payable amount

## Sector R, S and T

Sector R, Sector S and Sector T should each be checked separately.

Their payment structures, development and available plot sizes may differ.

Do not assume that a Sector P or Sector O price applies to R, S or T.

Use the dedicated sector plan and current written inventory for each location.

## Overseas Enclave plots

The Overseas Enclave also has active resale and paid-file inventory.

Current listings use different numbered Overseas Enclave references, including Enclave 4 and Enclave 6.

Recent examples include:

- 8 marla around PKR 30 lakh in Overseas Enclave 4
- 8 marla around PKR 34 lakh in Overseas Enclave 6
- 10 marla examples around PKR 32–36 lakh in Overseas Enclave 6

These are current seller asking examples and vary by enclave, payment status and development charges. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}

## Phase 1 vs Phase 2 plot comparison

Phase 1 and Phase 2 should not be compared only by headline price.

Phase 1 usually offers:

- established resale inventory
- more developed surroundings
- actual streets and houses to inspect
- possession-oriented buying
- higher land values in established areas

Phase 2 may offer:

- lower entry prices in some sectors
- newer booking or payment structures
- installment possibilities
- developing sectors
- longer investment horizons

A cheaper Phase 2 plot is not directly equivalent to an established Phase 1 possession plot.

## Plot-size comparison

When comparing plots, first match the size.

Then compare:

- exact dimensions
- phase
- block or sector
- development
- possession
- road width
- corner status
- main-road position
- dues
- payment completion
- total payable cost

A 5-marla plot in established Block C and a 5.56-marla Sector O plot serve very different market positions.

## What affects plot prices?

Plot prices can vary because of:

- phase
- block or sector
- plot size
- street
- road width
- corner position
- boulevard or main-road position
- park-facing position
- development
- possession
- outstanding installments
- development charges
- seller urgency
- current supply and demand

Avoid using one portal listing as the “price” of an entire block or sector.

## Cash vs installment plots

Cash and installment inventory should be compared separately.

A full-payment offer may look cheaper but require much more capital immediately.

An installment plot may have:

- higher total price
- down payment
- quarterly or monthly installments
- outstanding development charges
- future possession charges

Compare the total payable amount rather than only the booking amount.

## Fully paid vs partially paid plots

If buying resale inventory, confirm whether the property is:

- fully paid
- partially paid
- carrying outstanding installments
- carrying development charges
- carrying possession charges
- NDC-ready

An apparently cheap plot may have a large remaining balance.

Ask for the current ledger or written payable position before purchase.

## Corner and main-road plots

Special-location plots may carry premiums.

Typical examples include:

- corner
- main road
- boulevard
- park-facing
- open-facing
- green-facing

Ask for the exact premium before comparing with a standard internal plot.

## How to shortlist Phase 1 plots

For Phase 1:

1. Choose Block A, B, B-1 or C.
2. Choose the plot size.
3. Set a realistic budget.
4. Compare current same-size listings.
5. Check possession.
6. Check road and street.
7. Confirm dues.
8. Visit the plot.
9. Verify ownership.
10. Calculate total transaction cost.

Do not shortlist only from photographs or asking price.

## How to shortlist Phase 2 plots

For Phase 2:

1. Choose a sector or enclave.
2. Choose the plot size.
3. Decide between cash, installment or resale.
4. Ask for the exact plot or file status.
5. Match it to the sector plan.
6. Verify current development.
7. Check paid and unpaid amounts.
8. Confirm premiums.
9. Calculate final payable cost.
10. Verify the payment recipient and receipt process.

This avoids mixing very different types of inventory.

## Documents and plot verification

Before making a material payment, verify:

- seller identity
- ownership or allocation documentation
- exact plot or file reference
- payment history
- transfer eligibility
- outstanding dues
- map position
- possession status
- developer or society records where applicable

The property on paper should match the plot being shown.

## Site visit before buying

Where possible, visit the actual location before paying a token.

Check:

- approach route
- exact plot
- road width
- plot level
- drainage
- surrounding development
- neighboring houses or plots
- corner or premium position
- access to commercial or community facilities

For remote buyers, request a live walkthrough rather than relying only on old images.

## What a useful plot inquiry should include

To receive a useful shortlist, provide:

- Phase 1 or Phase 2
- block, sector or enclave
- preferred plot size
- budget
- investment or own-use purpose
- cash or installment preference
- possession requirement
- preferred location features

This makes it possible to compare relevant plots instead of sending generic listings.
